introduction.text: Equus Traiani was a colossal bronze equestrian statue of Emperor Trajan, erected in the Forum of Trajan in Rome. It symbolized Trajan's military victories and imperial power, and was a key monument in the forum.

history.description: The statue was erected between 112 and 114 CE, following Trajan's victories over the Dacians.
The statue remained intact into the IV century, as noted by Constantius II during his visit to Rome in 357 CE.

design.description: A colossal bronze equestrian statue, likely 10–12 meters tall, modeled after the statue of Marcus Aurelius.

art.description: The statue copied the pose of the horse and rider from the statue of Marcus Aurelius.
